description:
STATE AS OF 2026-09-18. The pre-op-t3l.9 determinism audit re-measured the
two bulk numbers and both survived:

  bulk bed     phi 0.5571 -> 0.5570  (0.0001, i.e. unchanged)
  HTR-10 core  phi 0.5732 -> 0.5732  (IDENTICAL; bed top 2.1686 vs 2.1687 m)

The angle of repose did NOT survive: 12.78 -> 14.09 deg, gap to LIGGGHTS
halving from 2.65 to 1.34 deg.

That is the predicted pattern -- BULK self-averaging quantities absorb the
last-bit perturbations the randomly-seeded HashMap introduced; SHAPE and
individual-configuration quantities follow individual pebbles and do not.

THE ONE NUMBER LEFT ON THE WRONG SIDE OF THAT LINE is the HTR-10 per-particle
agreement: 'median pebble 61 um apart, 99.93 % within 1 mm', recorded in
1db4e166b5, which is PRE-fix. It is an individual-configuration statistic, so
the principle predicts it moved. The crate's own CLAUDE.md already half-admits
this, noting the single 2.91e-2 m outlier is 'consistent with this mechanism'.

COMPLICATION, AND IT MUST BE HANDLED FIRST. Re-running tests/htr10_pebble_bed.rs
on 2026-09-18 REGENERATED reference-data/liggghts/htr10_settled_ours.csv --
27 554 rows, a 55 056-line diff in the working tree. That is arguably the right
outcome (the file now holds a bed from a reproducible build, where the old one
provably could not be regenerated), but it means:

  - the committed CSV no longer matches the bed the 61 um figure was measured
    against, so the old number cannot be reproduced even in principle;
  - whoever commits that CSV should say so explicitly in the message, because
    it silently re-baselines any comparison that reads it.

DELIVERABLE:
  1. Decide whether to commit the regenerated htr10_settled_ours.csv. If yes,
     say in the commit message that it re-baselines the per-particle comparison.
  2. Re-measure the per-particle median and the 'within 1 mm' fraction against
     LIGGGHTS' htr10_settled.csv on the fixed build.
  3. Correct docs/cross-code-summary.md and the CLAUDE.md maturity roster with
     the measured value, striking through 61 um rather than deleting it.

DO NOT quote 61 um as current until step 2 is done.
title: Re-measure HTR-10 per-particle 61 um median; htr10_settled_ours.csv was regenerated

description:
dwsim-libs has unit operations but no engine to connect them. A refinery is defined by its recycles (hydrogen recycle, pumparounds, stripper returns), so a flowsheet without recycle convergence is not a refinery.

SCOPE: material and energy stream types, a unit-operation enum covering the existing blocks, execution ordering with cycle detection, tear-stream selection, and an accelerated successive-substitution convergence loop (Wegstein or equivalent) with reportable residuals and iteration limits.

DESIGN RULES: unit operations dispatch through an enum, not Box<dyn>, so adding a block is a compile error at every match site. No lifetime parameters — share the property package with Arc.

ACCEPTANCE: a small flowsheet with a real recycle converges to a stated tolerance, with the residual history available for inspection rather than a silent converged/not-converged boolean.
title: refinery: flowsheet solver — sequential-modular execution with recycle convergence

description:
Working bead for the debugging campaign on op-s2dc's defect, now that the
regression is bisected to baf9408b (see op-s2dc's comment and op-ppmk).

The perturbation is not the defect. The defect is that the Edwards break cell
can reach the density floor at all, and that the energy equation then divides by
it.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS, from reading the assembly rather than guessing:

`step()` builds the energy equation as

    e_eqn = fvm::ddt_coeff_old(&rho_cont, &rho_old, &self.he, &he_old, dt) + ...
      diag[c]   += rho_cont[c] * V/dt
      source[c] += rho_old[c] * he_old[c] * V/dt
      source[c] -= V * div(phi, he)[c]

and `rho_cont` is built as `rho_old - dt*div_phi` and then CLAMPED:

    if rc.internal[c] < 1e-4 { rc.internal[c] = 1e-4; }

The module's own comment says the whole point of `rho_cont` is that discrete
continuity `(rho_cont - rho_old)/dt = -div(phi)` holds EXACTLY, so that the
`h_old*(rho_cont - rho_old)/dt` term cancels the `h*div(phi)` part of
`div(phi*h)` term for term. **The clamp breaks that identity.** Once it fires,
the cancellation is no longer exact, an uncancelled `h*div(phi)` of ordinary
magnitude remains in the source, and it is divided by a diagonal that has been
pinned at `1e-4 * V/dt`. That is a direct route to the recorded
h = -1.712179e10 J/kg, and it explains why the failure is at the break cell and
nowhere else.

So the candidate fix is NOT to move the floor. It is that a cell with no mass
has no meaningful specific enthalpy and must not have one solved for: hold `he`
there (identity row, source = he_old) instead of dividing by the floor.

SECOND OBSERVATION, also from reading rather than measuring. The 600 ms test
sets SolverMode::HybridAllMach (edwards_blowdown.rs:357), but the comparison
test runs Pimple FIRST (line 920) and the post-PETIR failure lands at 66.94 s,
inside that first run. If that holds up, PURE PIMPLE FAILS TOO and the KNP Mach
gating is not the cause -- which would make a Pimple-only run the right
baseline to carry the fix, and the Mach-gating work unnecessary. Verify before
relying on it.

METHOD: ablation, one change at a time, with every FAILED attempt written down
as well as the successful one. Log:
docs/edwards-post-petir-ablation.md
title: Edwards post-PETIR: ablation to find the energy-drain defect

description: carve_region's inside test is O(cells x all-hole-triangles), too slow for many pebbles/pins. Add per-hole bounding-box culling: precompute each hole bbox; a cell only runs the ray-parity inside test for holes whose bbox contains its centre (a cell is inside <=1 separated pebble, so cost drops to outer + ~1 hole). Unlocks pebble-bed / pin-lattice geometry. Plus a pebble_bed example (structured sphere packing -> carve_region -> snap -> quality) demonstrating the pebble-bed reactor coolant mesh. V&V: single-pebble result unchanged (bbox contains it); a lattice of N pebbles meshes in reasonable time with separated patches.
title: cfmesh: bbox-culled multi-hole carve + pebble-bed example (reactor scale)

design:
Child of the multi-thermo flowsheet epic (bn op-186o).


**The critical audit item, and it blocks the PH and PS bridges.**

Different packages may use different reference-state conventions. **A naive PH
bridge can be wrong even when both packages individually calculate sensible
enthalpies** — the error is invisible at each end and appears only across the
boundary, which is the worst failure mode available.

Explicitly investigate and document: enthalpy reference basis; formation
enthalpy treatment; ideal-gas reference; departure enthalpy; phase-change
contribution; reaction enthalpy conventions.

Define **either** a canonical convention **or** an explicit reference-state
translation. Add regression tests.

**Do not declare PH bridging correct until this is resolved.** A bridge that
silently shifts a datum produces a plausible temperature and a wrong energy
balance, and the flowsheet will converge on it.


## Constraints

Mature-crate refactor: preserve public constructors, deprecate rather than remove, regression tests before semantic changes. Do not implement AGR/Claus/the refinery here. `develop` only, no push to `main`.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: DESIGN 2026-09-05: canonical interchange is (P,T,x_phase,mole fractions), never enthalpy. Enthalpy is package-relative (reference-state dependent); (P,T,x,z) is physical. Phase fraction x is required because (P,T) is degenerate at saturation. Consequence: measure dH_ref = H_dest(P,T,x,z) - H_source(P,T,x,z) at the interchange state and define the PH bridge against the measured offset, rather than reconciling reference conventions symbolically. Caveat: a (P,T,x,z) handoff conserves state, not energy - correct for a T-fixing boundary (TP bridge), but an adiabatic stream needs the offset applied.

title: MultiThermo: Enthalpy reference-state reconciliation

design:
Child epic of the nuclear refinery programme (bn op-upme).

**Fidelity target: Crude estimate initially**

Scope **after** Claus.

```
Claus tail gas -> hydrogenation / hydrolysis -> H2S-containing gas
               -> absorption -> H2S recycle to Claus
                             -> treated tail gas
```

Track at least: **H2S; SO2; COS; CS2** where supported; sulfur recovery; fuel/H2
requirement.

COS and CS2 matter because they are the species that escape a Claus unit and
therefore dominate the residual sulfur term in the refinery-wide balance.

Depends on the SRU.

## Out of scope for this pass (programme-wide)

Do not: port DWSIM UI or graphical flowsheet objects; port CAPE-OPEN unless a
concrete backend requirement exists; reproduce .NET class architecture; make
DWSIM depend on Outram-FOAM; solve thousands of molecular species in the CDU;
implement molecular reconstruction before assay/pseudocomponent CDU works; call
a converged model validated without reference evidence; hide conservation
errors; push to `main`.
title: Refinery: Tail gas treatment unit

description:
Ported src/poly/quartic.rs from roots 0.0.8 (Mikhail Vorotilov, BSD-2-Clause) at the maintainer's direction: find_roots_quartic plus quartic_depressed, biquadratic, cubic_normalized, quadratic, linear and the Roots enum.

Fills a documented gap -- GSL's poly/ carries solve_quadratic.c and solve_cubic.c only, and solves higher degrees numerically by balanced QR on the companion matrix.

Deviations, all recorded in the file header: specialised to f64; upstream's panic on an unreachable arity returns the set unchanged instead; no slice subscripts; sqrt/cbrt/acos/cos via crate::real::Real.

Evidence: upstream's own assertions replayed and passing; worst scaled residual 3.655e-18 over 7 quartics; the ported cubic agrees with OpenFOAM's cubicEqn to 1.554e-15 over 5 cubics. No compiled-reference comparison is possible -- there is no GSL quartic to compare against, and verification-summary.md says so under 'What is NOT covered'.

Licence: BSD-2-Clause into GPL-3.0-only is one-way. Full notice and copyright retained in the file header. NOTICE, README and the crate CLAUDE.md were all corrected -- they previously asserted 'no code in PETIR is derived from either crate', which this port makes false.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Ported, tested and documented. 5 new tests pass; full petir suite green including no_panic_gate and verbatim_provenance. Cross-targets clean: thumbv7em-none-eabihf, wasm32-unknown-unknown, aarch64-linux-android --all-targets, --no-default-features. Measured (not asserted): worst scaled residual 3.655e-18; cubic cross-lineage agreement 1.554e-15.

One real bug was caught by reading upstream rather than trusting the draft: the first version of roots_via_depressed_quartic dropped the + 16*a4^2*(12*a0*a4 - 3*a1*a3 + a2^2) term from r. Confirmed the test suite catches it by re-injecting it (2 of 5 tests fail).

title: petir: closed-form quartic ported from the roots crate (BSD-2-Clause)
